documents.title: Receipt Of Trading Approval For 15,01,434 Equity Shares Of Face Value Rs. 2/- Each

analysis.summary: Bhagyanagar India Limited held its Q1 FY27 earnings conference call on July 28, 2026, reporting a turnover of over 700 crores and an EBITDA margin of 5.43%. Management noted that despite trade route disruptions and material shortages in the first two months affecting overall sales volumes to 5,200 tons, things normalized in June with strong dispatches and contributions from recently launched products. The company is proceeding with a corporate restructuring via Tieramet Limited for value unlocking and plans to execute a 40 crore capex across FY27 and FY28. Furthermore, management projects 12% to 15% volume growth for the full year and aims to achieve 5,000 crores in revenue by FY30. Bhagyanagar India Limited reported Q1FY27 financial performance with revenue from operations at Rs.

guidance.claim: The company expects to maintain EBITDA margins between 5% and 5.5% for the rest of the year.
guidance.quote: Going forward in the year, we hope to maintain the EBITDA margin between 5% and 5.5%.

guidance.claim: Export contribution for the year is estimated between 12% and 15%.
guidance.quote: 12-15% would be a good estimate for the year.

guidance.claim: Management is very confident of achieving 5,000 crores in revenue by FY30 regardless of copper prices.
guidance.quote: But we are very confident of 5,000 crores by FY30, whatever the copper price.

guidance.claim: The company aims to reach 5,000 crores in revenue by the year 2030.
guidance.quote: Our top line projection, as in earlier, this thing, has been project... we are aiming for 3,000 crores in the year 2030. That is, in 3 years, we are planning to reach 5,000 crores in the year 2030.

guidance.claim: Management targets a CAGR of between 20% to 25% for the next 3 to 4 years.
guidance.quote: 25% CAGR is our target for the next 3 to 4 years.

guidance.claim: Management is hopeful of maintaining a 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year.
guidance.quote: We are hopeful of maintaining 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year, and on an increased top line.

guidance.claim: The company expects a minimum volume growth of 15% to 20% every year.
guidance.quote: Between 15% to 20% should be our volume growth minimum every year.

guidance.claim: Management expects 20% volume growth and a 5% increase in prices out of the projected 25% growth.
guidance.quote: Out of the 25%, we are expecting 20% volume growth and 5% increase in prices.

guidance.claim: Management is planning to increase value-added products up to 66% by the end of next year.
guidance.quote: So, we've already reached around 62% at the end of quarter four, and we are planning to get this up to 66% by the end of next year.

demand_outlook.claim: India is highlighted as one of the fastest growing copper users globally, with consumption projected at 2.4 million metric tons by 2030.
demand_outlook.quote: As we can see, India is actually one of the fastest growing copper users in the world, with around 2.4 million metric tons projected to be consumed in India by 2030.

demand_outlook.claim: Secondary copper demand in India is expected to double in the next 5 years from 0.7 million metric tons to 1.4 million metric tons.
demand_outlook.quote: Out of this, if you look at the secondary copper demand, it is expected to double in the next 5 years, from 0.7 million metric tons to 1.4 million metric tons.

demand_outlook.claim: The recycled copper market in India is estimated by some reports to grow at a CAGR of about 12% to 13%.
demand_outlook.quote: The recycled copper market, by some estimates, should be growing in India at a CAGR of about 12-13%.

demand_outlook.claim: Growing sustainability focus and supply constraints are accelerating the transition from primary to recycled copper in India.
demand_outlook.quote: Growing sustainability focus and supply constraints are accelerating the transition from primary to recycled copper in India.

demand_outlook.claim: India is expected to become the second largest copper-consuming economy.
demand_outlook.quote: India is expected to become the second largest copper-consuming economy.

demand_outlook.claim: Copper consumption growth will mainly be driven by EV and automotive, power and electrification, and renewable energy sectors.
demand_outlook.quote: This growth will mainly be driven by three sectors, EV and automotive. Because, EV requires a lot more copper than regular cars, power and electrification is also a big growth factor, and renewable energy.

demand_outlook.claim: Global copper consumption is predicted to reach 50 million tonnes by 2050.
demand_outlook.quote: The world consumed around 26 million tonne of copper, which is predicted to become 50 million tonne by 2050, so this is almost doubling.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has finished adding a capacity of 35,000 metric tons which is now online.
capex_expansion.quote: We have also finished adding our capacity of 35,000 metric tons, which is online now.

capex_expansion.claim: Management proposed a capex of 40 crores over FY27 and FY28.
capex_expansion.quote: The management has proposed to do 40 crores of capex in the next 2 years, FY27 and FY28 and we are well on our way to achieve this.

capex_expansion.claim: Capacity expansion from 35,000 to 45,000 tons is projected for next year, most likely in June.
capex_expansion.quote: So, this has been projected for the next financial year. The exact timelines are still not there, but as of now, our expectation is between April and June of next year; more likely June next year. From 35,000 to 45,000 tons.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has proposed a capex of 40 crores in the next 2 years.
capex_expansion.quote: We are proposing about 40 crores capex in the next 2 years.

capex_expansion.claim: The company's capacity has reached 35,000 metric tonnes this year.
capex_expansion.quote: Our capacity has now reached 35,000 metric tonne this year, with the new, 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved its highest EBITDA margin of recent times at 5.43% and highest PAT margin at 2.87% in Q1 FY27.
margins_costs.quote: We have had our highest EBITDA margin of recent times at 5.43%, our highest PAT margin of 2.87%.

margins_costs.claim: Automobile and switchgear parts command the highest value addition.
margins_costs.quote: So, the highest value addition is in the automobile and switchgear part.

margins_costs.claim: Approximately 85% of inventory is hedged on the exchange.
margins_costs.quote: However, approximately 85% of the inventory which is there is hedged on the exchange.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved an EBITDA per kg of around 43 rupees for the year.
margins_costs.quote: Our EBITDA per kg for the year is around 43 rupees, which is very high compared to our peers, and as you can see, over the four quarters, our EBITDA per kg has been trending upwards.

margins_costs.claim: In quarter four, the company achieved an EBITDA of around 62 rupees per kg.
margins_costs.quote: With the quarter four, we achieved around 62 rupees per kg.

margins_costs.claim: Silver-bearing and tin-bearing bus bar products will give the company roughly about 10% EBITDA margins.
margins_costs.quote: So, we are, this product will give us roughly about 10%, EBITDA margins.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volumes for the quarter came down to 5,200 tons, of which 2,200 tons were achieved in June.
orders_capacity.quote: However, for the whole quarter, our volume has come down to 5,200 tons. But the good part of this is that 2,200 tons of the 5,200 tons has come only in the month of June.

orders_capacity.claim: The company achieved its highest share of value-added products sold this quarter at 63%.
orders_capacity.quote: We have also had our highest share of value-added products sold this quarter, which is 63% and our highest EBITDA per kg of 72 rupees.

orders_capacity.claim: Copper sales volume grew by 34% last year to reach 24,000 metric tonnes.
orders_capacity.quote: Last year, we did around 18,000 metric tonne of volume of copper sales. Which has gone up by 34% to, 2 24,000 metric tonne.

orders_capacity.claim: The company increased its capacity from 30,000 to 35,000 metric tonnes in March of this year.

capital_allocation.claim: A new company called Tieramet Limited will be formed as a wholly-owned subsidiary to house the copper business before being demerged.
capital_allocation.quote: We are going to form a new company called Tieramet Limited, which will be a wholly owned subsidiary of Bhagyanagar India. All the copper business will move from Bhagyanagar Copper to Tieramet and then Bhagyanagar Copper will be merged with Bhagyanagar India, while Tieramet is demerged outside.

capital_allocation.claim: The first round of fund raising has been finalized at 52 crores, expected in the bank in August.
capital_allocation.quote: So, we have just finalized the first round of raising, at 52 crores, which is finalized, and the money should be in the bank in the month of August.

capital_allocation.claim: Projected debt in 2030 is estimated between 300 and 350 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: So, our projection is showing that between 300 and 350 crores will be our debt in 2030.

capital_allocation.claim: Total fund raise via preferential allotment is Rs. 52.25 Crores.
The increase in equity was achieved entirely through retained earnings without any dilution.
capital_allocation.quote: And this increase in equity was not done through dilution, this was all done through retained earnings.

risks_headwinds.claim: Trade route disruptions and material shortages in the first two months caused turnover and volumes to drop initially.
risks_headwinds.quote: In the first two months, because of the disruption of all the trade routes and the shortage of material all over the country, while the turnover came down, we could take advantage of the situation by increasing our margins.

risks_headwinds.claim: A GST case involving a 17 crore input tax credit reversal was levied due to retrospective cancellation of a supplier's registration.
risks_headwinds.quote: Because of the retrospective cancellation of the registration of the supplier, the case has been put on us.

risks_headwinds.claim: Scrap coming from the Gulf has suddenly dried up, and shipping lines have been diverted.
risks_headwinds.quote: The scrap coming from Gulf, which is of a short duration, short lead time material, has suddenly dried up. And, the material which is coming from the rest of the world, the shipping lines have been diverted because a lot of shipping lines have a transit point in Dubai or somewhere in the Gulf before coming to India.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company's dependence on scrap from the Gulf is less than 5% of its material.
risks_headwinds.quote: We are dependent on scrap from Gulf to less than 5% of our material comes from Gulf.

risks_headwinds.claim: Exposure to the U.S. stands at 35%, which is the highest for a single country.
risks_headwinds.quote: And just because you've asked this question, I think I might as well say that our exposure to U.S. is 35%, which is the highest for a single country.

management_commitments.claim: The management plans to complete the corporate restructuring after the NCLT hearing scheduled for August 7.
management_commitments.quote: Currently, the NCLT hearing is scheduled for the 7th of August, after which we should soon be able to complete this restructuring.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to execute 40 crores of capex across FY27 and FY28.
management_commitments.quote: The management has proposed to do 40 crores of capex in the next 2 years, FY27 and FY28 and we are well on our way to achieve this.

management_commitments.claim: The second tranche of fundraising is expected around March after the demerger is completed.
management_commitments.quote: The second tranche will probably be around March, after the demerger is done, in the standalone copper unit.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to reach 5,000 crores in revenue by the year 2030.
management_commitments.quote: That is, in 3 years, we are planning to reach 5,000 crores in the year 2030.

management_commitments.claim: Management targets a CAGR of 25% for the next 3 to 4 years.
management_commitments.quote: 25% CAGR is our target for the next 3 to 4 years.

management_commitments.claim: Management is hopeful of maintaining a 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year.
management_commitments.quote: We are hopeful of maintaining 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year, and on an increased top line.

management_commitments.claim: Management plans to increase value-added products up to 66% by the end of next year.
management_commitments.quote: So, we've already reached around 62% at the end of quarter four, and we are planning to get this up to 66% by the end of next year.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
